data_section_full_text:
3.1 Data and sample


Following Hribar and Jenkins (2004) and Gleason et al. (2008), we use the GAO
(2002) sample of 845 firms that reported 919 restatements because of accounting
irregularities during January 1, 1997, to June 30, 2002. The GAO data include the
date of the restatement announcement, the reason for the restatement, and the
initiating party (the company, auditor, SEC, uncertain, and other). The GAO report
identifies nine possible reasons for the restatement: acquisitions and mergers; cost or
expense; in-process research and development (IPRD); reclassification; relatedparty transactions; restructuring, assets, or inventory; revenue recognition; securities

to focus on restatements resulting from accounting irregularities. <sup>14</sup>

From the 919 GAO restatements, we are able to identify 745 firms on CRSP,
representing 821 restatements. We require 36 months of returns before and after
each restatement announcement. <sup>15</sup> The requirement for 36 months of postannouncement returns limits the restatement sample to the period 1997 through
2001 because the IR factor return data cover up to 2004. This requirement decreases
the sample to 330 restatements, including 26 firms with multiple restatements. <sup>16</sup>

Firms with multiple restatements are included in the sample using 36 months of
return data before the first restatement and after the last restatement, excluding
returns between the restatement announcements. The final sample includes 299
restatement firms. The mean cumulative abnormal return (CAR) (day -3 to ?3) for
the restatement firms is -5.4%, significantly different from 0 at the 1% level,
consistent with prior research, which reports negative market returns for several
windows around the restatement announcement (Palmrose et al. 2004; Richardson
and Tuna 2002; Anderson and Yohn 2002; Hribar and Jenkins 2004). <sup>17</sup>
